sagrada_familia.name: Sagrada Família
aliases: temple expiatori de la sagrada familia
sagrada_familia.architect: Antoni Gaudí (took over from Francisco de Paula del Villar in 1883)
sagrada_familia.style: Gothic Revival combined with curvilinear Art Nouveau (Catalan Modernism)
sagrada_familia.consecrated: 7 November 2010, by Pope Benedict XVI, who proclaimed it a basilica
sagrada_familia.unesco_status: Nativity façade and Crypt declared UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005
sagrada_familia.status: Still under construction, funded solely by private donations and visitor entry fees
notable_facts: It is the tallest church in the world
Gaudí devoted the rest of his life to the project and is buried in its crypt
At Gaudí's death in 1926, less than a quarter of the project was complete
In 1936, anarchists set fire to the crypt during the Spanish Civil War, destroying part of Gaudí's original plans

casa_batllo.name: Casa Batlló
casa_batllo.location: Passeig de Gràcia, Eixample district, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
casa_batllo.architect: Antoni Gaudí (renovation of an existing 1877 building)
casa_batllo.unesco_status: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Works of Antoni Gaudí', inscribed 1984 (extended 2005)
casa_batllo.status: Completed, open to the public as a museum
notable_facts: The façade is covered in colorful trencadís (broken tile mosaic)
Locally nicknamed 'Casa dels ossos' (House of Bones) for its skeletal organic facade
The roof is often interpreted as representing the back of a dragon

park_guell.name: Park Güell
park_guell.location: La Salut neighbourhood, Gràcia district, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
park_guell.architect: Antoni Gaudí, commissioned by Eusebi Güell
park_guell.unesco_status: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Works of Antoni Gaudí', inscribed 1984
park_guell.status: Completed, operates as a public park (partly ticketed monumental zone)
notable_facts: Originally conceived as a residential garden-city development that was never completed as housing
Features the famous mosaic salamander ('el drac') at the main entrance

casa_mila.name: Casa Milà
casa_mila.location: Passeig de Gràcia, Eixample district, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain
casa_mila.unesco_status: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Works of Antoni Gaudí', inscribed 1984
casa_mila.status: Completed, open to the public as a museum and residential building
notable_facts: Nicknamed 'La Pedrera' (The Quarry) for its rough-hewn stone facade
Has no straight walls; the design is built around two large courtyards
The rooftop features sculptural chimneys often compared to medieval warriors
